Pregnancy Weight Gain Calculator

Compare current pregnancy weight gain with widely used singleton or twin-pregnancy total ranges based on pre-pregnancy BMI. It also shows a simple progress comparison, while leaving individual targets to prenatal care. The calculator selects the CDC-posted Institute of Medicine total-gain range using pre-pregnancy BMI and pregnancy type. A linear progress line is only a visual comparison, not a clinical trimester-specific growth model.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter pre-pregnancy height, pre-pregnancy weight, weight gained so far and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How pregnancy weight gain is calculated

The calculator selects the CDC-posted Institute of Medicine total-gain range using pre-pregnancy BMI and pregnancy type. A linear progress line is only a visual comparison, not a clinical trimester-specific growth model. For a singleton pregnancy with pre-pregnancy BMI 22, the reference total gain is 25–35 lb (about 11.3–15.9 kg).

Selects published total-gain range by pre-pregnancy BMI and singleton/twin pregnancy.
A worked example

Assumptions & useful context

Population reference only; individual pregnancy goals should be set with prenatal care.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

CDC: Pregnancy weight-gain recommendations

Frequently asked questions

Are these ranges a personal medical goal?

They are population recommendations; a prenatal clinician can individualize them.

Does the reference cover triplets?

No. Ask a maternity-care professional for a multiple pregnancy beyond twins.
